label: My home
description: Renting, repairs, moving, or keeping your home

needs.label: I may lose my home
needs.description: Eviction papers, a missed hearing, or a property-tax court case.

tools.label: Respond to an eviction case
tools.description: MADE helps you prepare a response and other papers after an eviction case is filed in court.

tools.label: Ask for another chance after a missed eviction hearing
tools.description: Explore asking the court to remove a default judgment and give you a new hearing.

tools.label: Explore an appeal or a delay of your eviction
tools.description: For a final eviction decision. The tool explains the steps for an appeal or a temporary delay.

tools.label: Respond to a property-tax court case
tools.description: For a tax-lien complaint about your property. Review the tool and the answer date on your papers.

needs.note: If you have court papers or a move-out date, check the deadlines now. This checkup does not file anything or extend a deadline.

needs.label: My rental home has problems
needs.description: Repairs, a lockout, utilities, or unwanted entry.

tools.label: Ask your landlord to make repairs
tools.description: Document problems, learn about repair options, and make letters or court papers with UpToCode.

tools.label: Ask the court for urgent help with your landlord
tools.description: Explore help with a lockout, utilities, unwanted entry, or serious repair problems.

needs.note: For a lockout or urgent housing problem, look at the help options promptly.

needs.label: I have trouble moving or getting my deposit back
needs.description: An old eviction record, a paid judgment, a housing search, or a deposit.

tools.label: See if you can keep an old eviction case private
tools.description: The interview checks whether your eviction record may qualify for sealing.

tools.label: Show the court you paid an eviction judgment
tools.description: For tenants who paid the full judgment in a nonpayment eviction case.

tools.label: Ask for your security deposit back
tools.description: Make a demand letter if your landlord has not returned your deposit after you moved out. The tool explains when it applies.

tools.label: Keep a record of your housing search
tools.description: Track places you contacted or applied to when a court or housing authority gives you a deadline to move.

needs.label: I need a housing change because of a disability
needs.description: A change to a rule, policy, or the way your landlord does things.

tools.label: Request a disability accommodation from your landlord
tools.description: Make a letter explaining a disability-related change you or someone in your household needs.

needs.label: I disagree with a request about an old eviction case
needs.description: Someone asked to seal the record or mark the judgment as paid.

tools.label: Respond to a petition about an eviction record or judgment
tools.description: For a landlord or tenant in the original eviction case who wants to object to a request to seal it or mark the judgment satisfied.

needs.note: This option is for responding to someone else’s petition. If you want to seal your own eviction record, choose the moving or records situation instead.

label: Money, benefits & work
description: Bills, food benefits, health coverage, Social Security, or your job

needs.label: Debt collectors keep contacting me
needs.description: Calls or letters from a collection agency.

tools.label: Ask a debt collector to stop contacting you
tools.description: Make a letter to a collection agency. The tool can also help explain certain protections for your income.

needs.note: A letter to a debt collector does not answer a lawsuit or erase the debt. If you have court papers, check their deadlines.

needs.label: I have a problem with benefits
needs.description: MassHealth, Social Security repayments, or reporting changes.

tools.label: Challenge a MassHealth decision
tools.description: Explore requesting a hearing about coverage, benefits, eligibility, or a delay in acting on your application.

tools.label: Ask for relief from a Social Security overpayment
tools.description: Explore a waiver or a lower repayment rate. This tool is not an appeal of whether the overpayment happened.

tools.label: Report a life change to Social Security
tools.description: Make a report about changes such as your address, income, work, or living arrangements if you get SSI or SSDI.

tools.label: Track spending from a child’s SSI account
tools.description: For a parent or representative payee tracking spending from a dedicated account for a child’s back benefits.

needs.note: If you received a benefits notice, check its deadlines. These tools cover particular benefit problems, not every application or appeal.

needs.label: I need a change at work because of a disability
needs.description: Help doing your job, applying for a job, or using workplace benefits.

tools.label: Request a disability accommodation at work
tools.description: Make a letter asking your employer for a change related to a disability.

needs.label: My new car keeps needing repairs
needs.description: A new car bought or leased from a Massachusetts dealer.

tools.label: Explore a final repair request for a new car
tools.description: The tool explains the new-car Lemon Law requirements and helps make a letter to the dealership.

needs.label: I want to estimate my food benefits
needs.description: An estimate of Massachusetts SNAP benefits.

tools.label: Estimate a monthly SNAP benefit amount
tools.description: A calculator for people familiar with SNAP rules, or working with a helper who is. It provides an estimate, not an application or a decision about eligibility.

needs.label: I am suing someone to collect a debt
needs.description: Court paperwork to verify the other person’s address.

tools.label: Verify an address in a debt collection case
tools.description: For the person suing to collect certain debts, such as credit-card or loan payments. This affidavit supports an existing case; it does not start a lawsuit or respond to one against you.

label: Children, family & safety
description: Caregiving, child support, getting married, or safety at home

needs.label: I need protection from someone
needs.description: Abuse, an unsafe home, or a restraining order you asked for.

tools.label: Explore a restraining order for domestic abuse
tools.description: For abuse involving certain family, household, or intimate relationships. The tool explains who can use it.

tools.label: Ask to change an order you requested
tools.description: For the person who asked for an existing 209A order and wants to change or end it.

tools.label: Ask for a spouse or co-parent to leave your home
tools.description: Explore this option if you have an existing family court case and need protection for you or your children.

needs.note: If you are in immediate danger, call 911 if it is safe. This checkup does not request emergency help. For abuse outside these relationships, other protections may be available.

needs.label: A child needs someone to care for them
needs.description: Temporary help, guardianship, or a change to a guardian.

tools.label: Find the right kind of care for a child
tools.description: Start here to compare caregiving permission, a temporary agent, and guardianship. It directs you to the relevant forms.

tools.label: Have a say in a child’s guardianship case
tools.description: For an existing case: tell the court whether you agree or disagree, or ask to take part.

tools.label: Ask to remove or replace a child’s guardian
tools.description: Explore asking the court to remove a guardian of a minor.

tools.label: Tell the court about other cases involving a child
tools.description: A supporting affidavit for a custody, guardianship, or related family case. Check whether your main interview already includes it before making another copy.

needs.label: I am struggling with child support payments
needs.description: Back support, collections, or a license affected by child support.

tools.label: Explore help with child support collection problems
tools.description: Learn about options with DOR/CSE, including back support and some license or collection problems. This tool does not change the amount of your court-ordered support.

needs.label: I need help with a family or care case
needs.description: DCF disability support, a CRA case, a family court request, or an adult guardian report.

tools.label: Ask DCF for disability-related support
tools.description: For a parent or caregiver who needs changes to meetings, services, or other parts of working with DCF.

tools.label: Ask to dismiss a Child Requiring Assistance case
tools.description: For a child who already has a CRA case in court.

tools.label: Make a request in an existing family court case
tools.description: Ask the judge for a decision in a Probate and Family Court case. This does not start a new divorce or custody case.

tools.label: Complete an adult guardian’s care report
tools.description: For an appointed adult guardian’s 60-day or annual care report. This does not establish guardianship or make an initial report.

tools.label: Tell the court about other cases involving a child
tools.description: A supporting affidavit for a custody, guardianship, or related family case. Check whether your main interview already includes it before making another copy.

needs.label: I need to get married without waiting
needs.description: Ask about skipping the usual marriage waiting period.

tools.label: Ask to waive the marriage waiting period
tools.description: Prepare a request for permission to marry without the usual waiting period. The tool explains the requirements and signatures needed.

label: School
description: Learning needs, school records, translation, or interpretation

needs.label: My child may need special education
needs.description: Ask the school to evaluate your child’s learning needs.

tools.label: Request a special education evaluation
tools.description: Make a letter asking the school to evaluate your child’s needs.

needs.label: I disagree with the school’s evaluation
needs.description: Explore asking for an independent evaluation.

tools.label: Request an independent evaluation
tools.description: For a parent or guardian who disagrees with the school’s special education evaluation.

needs.label: I need school records
needs.description: Request a complete copy of a student’s records.

tools.label: Request school records
tools.description: Make a request for a complete student record.

needs.label: I need translation or an interpreter at school
needs.description: Report a problem getting language help from the school.

tools.label: Report a school language-access problem
tools.description: Make a complaint about a school’s failure to provide required translation or interpretation.

label: Records & court
description: A fresh start, court paperwork, or an appeal

needs.label: I want a fresh start with my records or name
needs.description: A juvenile record, an old eviction, or a legal name change.

tools.label: See if you can seal a juvenile record
tools.description: The interview checks whether you can seal a Massachusetts juvenile record. It is not a general adult criminal-record sealing tool.

tools.label: See if you can keep an old eviction case private
tools.description: The interview checks whether your eviction record may qualify for sealing.

tools.label: Explore a legal name change for an adult
tools.description: Prepare a petition for an adult name change in Massachusetts.

tools.label: Explore a legal name change for a child
tools.description: For a parent or guardian preparing a petition to change a child’s name.

needs.label: I need help taking part in court
needs.description: Court costs, an interpreter, or finding the right court.

tools.label: Ask to waive court fees and costs
tools.description: Explore asking the court to waive costs you cannot afford.

tools.label: Tell the court you need an interpreter
tools.description: Make a notice that you need an interpreter for your court hearings.

tools.label: Find a Massachusetts court
tools.description: Look up which court serves a location.

needs.label: I missed a court hearing
needs.description: A judgment entered without you, including an eviction hearing.

tools.label: Ask to reopen a case when you did not get notice
tools.description: For a default judgment after you missed a hearing because you did not get notice.

tools.label: Ask for another chance after a missed eviction hearing
tools.description: For tenants with a reason for missing their eviction hearing and a defense to the eviction.

needs.note: Check your court papers promptly. This checkup does not file anything or extend a deadline.

needs.label: I want a court decision reviewed or paused
needs.description: A decision you disagree with, or want put on hold.

tools.label: Explore review of a decision before the case is final
tools.description: Ask a single justice of the Appeals Court to review certain trial-court decisions that are not final judgments. The tool explains the limits.

tools.label: Ask the Appeals Court to pause a judgment
tools.description: Explore a stay after the trial court has denied your request to pause the judgment. Read the tool’s instructions about the notice of appeal.

tools.label: Ask the Appeals Court to reconsider its decision
tools.description: For a decision by the Appeals Court, not simply a change in your circumstances or a trial-court decision. The tool explains when it can be used.

tools.label: Explore an appeal or a delay of your eviction
tools.description: For a final eviction decision. The tool explains the steps for an appeal or a temporary delay.

needs.note: Review and appeal deadlines can be short. These are different options for different stages of a case, not a checklist. Check your court papers and each tool’s instructions promptly.

needs.label: I need help with papers for an appeal
needs.description: Starting the next stage, writing a brief, or asking for more time.

tools.label: Prepare a civil appeal entry form
tools.description: For a civil appeal after you receive a Notice of Assembly. This is not the notice of appeal filed in the trial court.

tools.label: Give the Appeals Court information about your case
tools.description: Prepare the statement describing your case and the people involved.

tools.label: Explain your appeal in an informal brief
tools.description: For a person representing themselves who is appealing a decision. Check the tool’s instructions about the informal brief program.

tools.label: Reply to an appeal in an informal brief
tools.description: For a person representing themselves who needs to respond to the other side’s appeal.

tools.label: Ask for more time to file your appeal brief
tools.description: Request an extension for a brief in an existing Appeals Court case. This does not extend the deadline to start an appeal.

tools.label: Make another request in the Appeals Court
tools.description: For a motion not covered by a more specific Appeals Court tool. Read the examples and instructions before choosing it.

needs.note: You may need only some of these papers. This checkup is not a complete guide to starting an appeal and does not extend any deadline.

needs.label: I need to complete other court paperwork
needs.description: An appearance, a cover sheet, or permission for a court-record check.

tools.label: Tell the court you are taking part in a case
tools.description: Prepare a Notice of Appearance for a Massachusetts Trial Court case. It does not replace an answer or other papers you may need.

tools.label: Prepare a cover sheet for a Superior Court civil case
tools.description: Provide basic case information to go with your civil filing. A cover sheet alone does not make your legal claim.

tools.label: Give permission for the court to check your record
tools.description: Prepare a CARI form when it is needed for a case such as guardianship, adoption, or a name change. This does not seal a record.
